//: Guard policy for the central-command repo. Logic lives in web-storefront-copilot-config/scripts; the rules live here.
//layers: Dependencies point DOWNWARD ONLY: a layer may import equal or lower levels, never higher. Enforced by arch-check.mjs.

layers.name: core
layers.//: DESIGN.md §19 invariant 6: core imports no vendor package, no connector, and no Node builtin. Clock and id generation are injected.

layers.name: tasks
layers.//: DESIGN.md §19 invariant 1: tasks are pure. They receive connectors through context; they never import one.

layers.name: stalls
layers.//: The stall engine is a pure function of (mirror snapshot, thresholds, now). No I/O, injected clock, so every rule in the catalog is table-testable.

layers.name: store
layers.//: All SQL is confined here. Nothing above this layer knows the storage engine.

layers.name: sync
layers.//: Orchestrates connectors into the store and derives events. Same level as executor: may use store and connectors, never a task or the dashboard.

//vendorSdks: Empty today: the project has zero runtime dependencies (node:sqlite is built in). Add an SDK here the moment one is introduced, or vendor placement goes unchecked.

purityPatterns.why: reads the clock directly — inject a clock so staleness and expiry tests are deterministic
reads the environment directly — pass config in

bannedPatterns.what: `as any` erases the type system at exactly the boundary that needed checking
suppressing the type checker hides the defect instead of fixing it
disabling the linter inline — fix the code or change the rule deliberately
use the store-backed logger so output is auditable and retained
DESIGN.md §7 denylist: these must exist ONLY in the compiled-in denylist and its tests, never in an executable code path
